                    ### Question
                    Question linked to the image nº5 62-year-old man, smoker of 20 cigarettes a day for 30 years and hypertensive, who comes to the clinic because of pain when walking in the gluteal area that begins at a distance of 300 meters and disappears with rest at 5 minutes. An Ankle / Arm index is made whose image is attached. Which is the diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Critical ischemia of right lower limb.
opb. Acute ischemia due to arterial embolism.
opc. Chronic ischemia due to left iliac occlusion.
opd. Leriche syndrome due to bilateral iliac occlusion.
ope. Radiculopathy

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's history of smoking and hypertension increases the risk of peripheral artery disease. The presentation of pain when walking in the gluteal area that improves with rest is suggestive of intermittent claudication. The Ankle/Arm index showing reduced blood flow to the lower limb is indicative of peripheral artery disease. The diagnosis is critical ischemia of the right lower limb, supported by the clinical presentation and test findings.
